name: Kakatiya Temples
theme: The star-shaped stone temples of the Kakatiya dynasty in Telangana, from UNESCO-listed Ramappa to the walled shrines of Ghanpur and the carved temple of Pillalamarri
description: From Warangal, the Kakatiya dynasty ruled much of the Telugu country between the twelfth and fourteenth centuries and left behind temples of a distinctive genius — star-shaped platforms, black basalt polished like metal, and pillars turned as if on a lathe. This circuit joins four of the finest: the three-shrined Thousand Pillar Temple of 1163 at Hanamkonda; the Rudreshwara temple of 1213 at Palampet, named for its sculptor Ramappa and inscribed by UNESCO in 2021; Kota Gullu at Ghanpur, a walled complex of some twenty shrines raised in the 1230s, only a short drive from Ramappa; and Pillalamarri, farther off near Suryapet, where the Erakeswara temple is celebrated for its fine carving. The first three sit in the countryside around Warangal and can be seen in an easy day; Pillalamarri makes a natural extension.
